content.key_idea: Every model node resolves a request locally by chaining two yes/no checks, cache hit then reputation, both of which fall back to the same load-balance-factor rule when unsatisfied, so PlanetServe forwards requests without any central router.
content.reading_order: top to bottom through the two decision diamonds, following YES down the left column and both NO branches merging right into shared action boxes, then diagonally out to the model-node cluster on the right

evidence: The forwarding logic, illustrated in Fig. 4, is designed to consider both KV cache reusing and load balancing objectives.
Its main objectives are to prevent overload and ensure each model serves enough requests to establish a reputation score.
If the search result is a match, the HR-tree identifies a list of model nodes that hold reusable KV caches.

summary: This figure diagrams PlanetServe's decentralized overlay-forwarding logic, executed locally by every model node on each incoming request. A first decision diamond asks whether the request's prompt is a cache hit by searching the node's Hash-Radix tree (HR-Tree); on a NO, the request is forwarded to the model node with the lowest load-balance (LB) factor, prioritizing load balancing over cache reuse. On a YES, a second diamond checks whether any cache-hit node's reputation score exceeds a threshold; if none qualifies, forwarding again falls back to the lowest-LB-factor node, otherwise the node picks the lowest-LB-factor node among the qualifying cache-hit candidates and forwards the request to it. A side icon cluster shows the pool of model nodes serving the same LLM, which periodically synchronize their HR-Tree state and request counts so every node's local decision reflects a consistent, if occasionally slightly stale, view of the group.
